evidence.locator: SI Figs41–48 at PDF/printedpp40–47, individually visually inspected; DN5 enlarged with pdftoppm at600dpi but source remains low resolution

objects.name: DN1
objects.note: Fig41,p40: staggered open strip of numbered helix circles, auxiliary circles on one side; long flattened colored strand paths with deletions/insertions. No closed barrel geometry is directly encoded by the flat cross-section alone.

objects.name: DN2
objects.note: Fig42,p41: similar staggered open-strip cross-section and visibly shorter flattened routing thanDN1. Exact shared strand/sequence identity not verified.

objects.name: DN3
objects.note: Fig43,p42: broader staggered strip with two isolated protruding numbered circles near center; colored paths include crosslinks across central gap and red deletion marks.

objects.name: DN4
objects.note: Fig44,p43: narrower staggered cross-section strip with auxiliary circles and elongated flattened routing. Small axis labels limit exact numerical transcription.

objects.name: DN5
objects.note: Fig45,p44: very small ring-like cross-section icon above long narrow routing panel. Enlarged600dpi crop remains pixelated; exact labels and connectivity cannot be verified. The prior mainFig2 appearance must not be called planar: a rectangular projection does not establish planarity.

objects.name: DN6
objects.note: Fig46,p45: numbered0–23 cross-section arranged in a compact ring/bundle-like pattern around an empty region; flattened paths show terminal scaffold returns and multiple strand crossovers. Full topology/native lattice assignment still requires verification.

objects.name: DN7
objects.note: Fig47,p46: numbered0–47 cross-section with filled/unfilled circles arranged in a multirow staggered pattern; flattened colored strands and blue returns are visible. Fig2 rod-like appearance is insufficient to infer final arrangement from this unrolled diagram.

objects.name: DN8
objects.note: Fig48,p47: twelve separated six-circle cross-section groups numbered through71, with long connections between routing blocks; mainFig2 depicts an octahedral frame. Local bundle layout does not on its own resolve catalog eligibility or final inter-bundle routing.

limitations: Visual review, not reconstruction or validation of native connectivity. Source sequence mappings, variant identities and full lattice decisions remain open.
